item: The guard's drain copies the log with PASSIVE before it asks for the gate, so a gate a long writer holds no longer costs it the copy
summary: Three of the ten kept checkpoint events of 16 Oct were skipped, WriteGateBusy, 30 s while the log grew from 1.4 to 1.6 GB. checkpoint_wal(passive_without_gate=True), passed only by the guard's drain (a source-level test pins that), runs PASSIVE first with no gate and then asks for TRUNCATE exactly as before; a gate that stays busy leaves a record that says skipped AND carries passive and page_size, the journal says passive-only, the pin report is built from it and the log line says how far behind the oldest reader holds the log. The pass boundary and the restore's checkpoint keep both steps inside the gate. It does not shrink the file, free a log a reader pins, or move the frames of an open transaction. 12 tests; 10 mutants killed by a named test, one removed as an equivalent line (the busy timeout PASSIVE never uses).
